parts.label: a
parts.ask: A histogram shows the number of hours, \(T\), that 90 patients stay in hospital after an operation. Its bars are 0 to 4 hours (frequency density 2.5), 4 to 7 (3), 7 to 12 (4.2), 12 to 16 (4), 16 to 20 (3.5) and 20 to 40 (1). Use the histogram to estimate \(\mathrm{P}(10 < T < 30)\).

steps.why: Frequency = width \(\times\) density. Only 10 to 12 of the 7 to 12 bar counts, and 20 to 30 of the 20 to 40 bar.

parts.label: b
parts.ask: The 90 times have mean 14.9 hours and standard deviation 9.3 hours. Tomas suggests \(T \sim \mathrm{N}(14.9,\ 9.3^2)\). With reference to the histogram, state, giving a reason, whether or not Tomas' model could be suitable.

steps.text: The histogram rises to a peak and then tails off slowly to the right: it is positively skewed.
steps.why: Give a reason about shape: symmetry or bell shape.

parts.answerText: Not suitable: the histogram is not symmetric (it is skewed), but a normal distribution is symmetric.

check.answers: reasoning: the shape of the histogram against a normal model

parts.label: c
parts.ask: Xiang models the frequency polygon by \(y = kx\mathrm{e}^{-x}\), \(0 \leq x \leq 4\), where \(x\) is in tens of hours. Use algebraic integration to show that \(\displaystyle\int_0^n x\mathrm{e}^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x = 1 - (n+1)\mathrm{e}^{-n}\).

parts.label: d
parts.ask: Show that, for Xiang's model, \(k = 99\) to the nearest integer.
parts.method: Area under the curve = total frequency

steps.why: The area under a frequency polygon is the total frequency, 90.

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.ask: Estimate \(\mathrm{P}(10 < T < 30)\) using Xiang's curve \(y = 99x\mathrm{e}^{-x}\) and the answer to part (c).

steps.why: \(x\) is in tens of hours: 10 to 30 hours is \(x = 1\) to \(3\).
That is a number of patients: divide by 90.

parts.label: f
parts.ask: The researcher decides to use Xiang's curve to model \(\mathrm{P}(a < T < b)\). State one limitation of Xiang's model.

steps.text: The curve is only defined for \(0 \leq x \leq 4\), that is, up to 40 hours.

parts.answerText: Some patients might stay in hospital longer than 40 hours, and the model cannot give probabilities for those times.

check.answers: a limitation of the model, in context: no number to compare
